PORTFOLIO DISCOVERY / EMPLOYER PERSONAS

Two employers.
Two lenses on impact.

Who is my portfolio for? These two employer personas help me plan evidence for an AI forward-deployed engineering career at companies such as Google and Accenture.

Meet the personas ↓

Fictional personas · Source-informed hypotheses · November 17, 2026

PURPOSE & EVIDENCE

Design for a reviewer.
Stay honest about the research.

Maya and Jordan are invented names, not real employees. Their goals, frustrations, review journeys, and success measures are portfolio-design hypotheses. No employer interviews or hiring validation have been conducted.

The official role examples below inform the company context. They are experienced-role benchmarks, not verified 2029 openings or proof of my eligibility. My profile remains Information Systems at NJIT, expected graduation January 2029.

PERSONA P1 / GOOGLE

M
HYPOTHETICAL TECHNICAL REVIEWER

Maya — AI Engineering Hiring Manager

Company context: Google Cloud · Customer-facing applied AI engineering

Goal

Assess whether I can reason about software, explain design tradeoffs, and grow toward building dependable AI integrations with customers.

Review scenario

Maya opens my portfolio after an early-career application or introduction. She wants a short route from the project summary to code, setup instructions, and evidence of how I check behavior.

Needs

  • Clear project architecture, data flow, and API boundaries.
  • Code evidence and reproducible setup or evaluation instructions.
  • Failure cases, limitations, and a clear account of my contribution.
  • Cloud or deployment experience labeled accurately.

Frustrations

“AI-powered” claims without implementation evidence; demos without limitations; unclear personal ownership; and screenshots that cannot be traced to source.

What my portfolio should show

Lead with one inspectable technical case study. Include the problem, architecture, code links, tests or evaluation, and tradeoffs. If a cloud deployment is only planned, say so.

Current evidence: Python calculator code, an Express server, and reproducible research tooling provide foundations. They do not establish production AI delivery.

Next evidence to build: A small documented AI integration with evaluation cases and a deployment explanation.

Persona user story

“As a technical hiring manager, I want to inspect the implementation and evaluation of a relevant project so I can assess the candidate’s engineering reasoning.”

Proposed usability target

A reviewer can find source code and a documented check within 60 seconds of opening a featured case study. This is a design target, not a measured result.

Official company context and its limits

Google’s Forward Deployed Engineer IV, Applied AI role describes customer AI integrations, evaluation, observability, and reusable engineering patterns. It is labeled advanced and lists eight years of software-development experience. It serves as a longer-term skills reference, not an entry-level match.

Google Careers · Official role example ↗ · Description retrieved November 17, 2026. Availability and requirements can change.

PERSONA P2 / ACCENTURE

J
HYPOTHETICAL CLIENT-EMBEDDED ENGINEERING REVIEWER

Jordan — AI Delivery Hiring Manager

Company context: Accenture · Enterprise AI implementation

Goal

Assess whether I can connect a business problem to technical work, collaborate with stakeholders, and explain how a solution could be supported after handoff.

Review scenario

Jordan opens my portfolio while considering developing engineering talent for customer-facing work. The first questions are what problem I addressed, what I contributed, and what evidence supports the result.

Needs

  • A clear problem statement, intended users, and project scope.
  • Evidence of requirements, feedback, and changes made.
  • Defined success criteria with honest measured or unmeasured status.
  • Implementation details, handoff notes, and team attribution.

Frustrations

Tool lists without a user problem; invented ROI or client outcomes; team projects presented as solo work; and a polished demo without operational context.

What my portfolio should show

Use a case study with problem → requirements → implementation → checks → limitations → handoff. Explain where communication changed the work.

Current evidence: Hospitality, leadership, presentations, and team projects can illustrate transferable communication skills. They do not establish client-embedded AI deployment.

Next evidence to build: A scoped workflow prototype with documented tester feedback, an evaluation rubric, and a clear handoff guide.

Persona user story

“As a client-embedded engineering hiring manager, I want to understand the user problem, delivery decisions, and documented outcome so I can assess the candidate’s potential to work with client teams.”

Proposed usability target

A reviewer can identify the intended user, my contribution, and the result’s evidence or unmeasured status within 90 seconds. This target has not been tested.

Official company context and its limits

Accenture’s Forward Deployed AI Engineer example is a mid-level Associate Manager role focused on embedded production engineering. It emphasizes operational reliability, business outcomes, enterprise integration, and reusable client handoffs. The posting specifically requires client-embedded delivery experience; student or team-only work does not substitute for it.

Accenture Careers · Official role R00339257 ↗ · Description reviewed November 17, 2026. This role is engineering-focused; the portfolio’s consulting title does not redefine its requirements.

WORKED EXAMPLE / THEME THROUGH TASK

One story.
Two reviewer perspectives.

Theme T2: Build trust through evidence.

↓ Epic E4: Project case-study screen.

↓ Story S4.1: As a portfolio reviewer, I want to understand a project’s problem, approach, and result so I can assess relevant engineering and delivery reasoning.

Acceptance criteria: The case study shows a user problem, a technical diagram or equivalent explanation, relevant source links, a documented check, and evidence-labeled outcomes. Missing evidence is explicit. Ownership follows S4.2.

  1. S4.1.T1: Select a project with inspectable evidence.
  2. S4.1.T2: Document the problem, implementation flow, and source links.
  3. S4.1.T3: Add verification evidence and distinguish observed results from proposed benefits.
  4. S4.1.T4: Review the case study using both persona perspectives.

Dependency: S3.2 source evidence. Priority: Must. Target: Iteration 2. Status: Proposed.

Updating documentation does not complete the implementation stories. The two-iteration plan and definition of done remain on the portfolio plan page.

VALIDATION / ASSUMPTIONS TO TEST

Use the personas.
Then challenge them.

Ask willing classmates or mentors to follow the two reviewer journeys. Record what they find and where they get stuck; do not treat those participants as Google or Accenture representatives. Employer interviews would be needed to validate company-specific assumptions.
